## Own the software your company runs on.

Our engineers replace the software you rent with systems you own.

Book a 15-minute call
See how it happens

## Every problem got a subscription.

One tool for forms. One for approvals. One for the spreadsheet nobody trusts. Each one cheap on its own, each one asking your team to work its way.

## Then the bill came due.

$9,455 Median SaaS spend per employee, every year. Zylo, 2026 SaaS Management Index

Prices rise over 12% a year, and close to half of the seats you pay for sit underused.

## Meanwhile, building got cheap.

32% Of companies skipped a software purchase because AI coding tools let them build it. McKinsey, The state of AI in 2026

What took a team a quarter now takes a few engineers a few weeks. The math that made renting the default has flipped.

## So we replace what bends your process.

We retire the tools that make your team work their way, and build one system that works yours. The tools that do one job well, you keep.

## What we build.

Four kinds of system. Each runs on your stack, in your accounts, and replaces something you rent today.

### Workflow automation

Moves records between the systems you keep, on rules you set. An order arrives by email, gets checked, and lands in the ERP without anyone retyping it.

Replaces: workflow tools, copy-paste, the integration nobody maintains.

### AI agents

Reads the inbox, the PDFs and the tickets, then drafts the reply, the quote or the order. A person approves before anything leaves the building.

Replaces: hours in inboxes, seat-priced AI add-ons.

### Team software

One system shaped around how one team actually works: their records, their statuses, their approvals. No workarounds, no second spreadsheet.

Replaces: trackers, portals, the spreadsheet one person understands.

### Knowledge base

Your policies, manuals and past decisions, searchable in plain words. Every answer cites the document and the section it came from.

Replaces: wiki seats, asking the longest-serving person.

## How it works.

Three phases. You can stop after any of them and keep what you have.

### Audit.

2 weeks, fixed fee.

Week 1 We sit with the team doing the work. We list every tool, every seat, and the job each one really does.

Week 2 We time the work, pick what to replace first, and write a fixed-price spec with the payback.

You get the spec. It is yours to keep, even if you never build with us.

### Replace.

3 to 6 weeks, fixed price.

Build On your stack, connected to the systems you keep. Code goes to your repository from day one.

Test On your past cases, side by side with the old tools, until your team signs off.

Switch We move the data, switch the system on, and cancel the seats it replaced.

You get a working system, the code, and a smaller software bill.

### Run.

Monthly, flat fee.

Watch We monitor every run and fix what breaks, usually before you notice.

Improve Small changes ship as your process changes. No change requests, no tickets.

Report Each month: what ran, what was fixed, and the numbers against week one.

You can stop any month. The system keeps running in your accounts.

## What own it means. In writing.

Every engagement ships under the same five terms.

01 Your repository
The code lives in your GitHub from the first commit.

02 Your cloud
It runs in your accounts, on your bill, not ours.

03 Your data
It stays in your systems and trains nothing.

04 No seats
No per-user pricing. Add a hundred people for nothing.

05 No lock-in
If we part ways, you keep everything, with a runbook.

## Questions, answered.

Who maintains it after launch?
We do, on the monthly run plan. Or your own team does, with the runbook and the code we hand over. Either way it lives in your accounts.

Is it secure?
It runs in your cloud, under your security policies. Each connector gets only the access its job needs, and every action is logged with who approved it.

What happens if we stop working together?
Nothing switches off. You keep the code, the accounts, the data and a runbook. Another engineer can pick it up on day one.

How do you price?
A fixed fee for the audit, a fixed price for the build, quoted in the spec before you commit, then a flat monthly fee to run it. Never per seat.

What will you not replace?
Tools that do one job well for everyone: email, payroll, your accounting ledger. We replace the tools that make your team bend its process to fit.

Where does AI come in?
Two places. Agents that draft work for a person to approve, and AI-assisted engineering, which is why a build takes weeks instead of quarters.

Who is this for?
US companies of 50 to 500 people whose teams spend their days between too many tools.

## Bring us your software bill.

We will tell you which subscription to replace first, and what it costs to own instead.
